https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Huge fire breaks out on industrial estate near Wembley stadium London Large fire near Wembley Stadium disrupts tube and rail services About 125 firefighters tackle blaze at Neasden waste facility as nearby Amazon warehouse is evacuated Nadeem Badshah and agencies Fri 28 Aug 2026 17.47 EDT First published on Fri 28 Aug 2026 14.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A large fire broke out at a waste facility close to Wembley Stadium in north-west London, disrupting tube and train lines in the area. Twenty fire engines and about 125 firefighters were sent to tackle the blaze at a mixed-waste facility on an industrial estate in Neasden, less than a mile from the venue. There was no service on the entire Metropolitan line, which runs close to the blaze, and no service between Wembley Park and West Hampstead on the Jubilee line, with severe delays on the rest of the line, Transport for London said. Rail services into London Marylebone were also disrupted. View image in fullscreen About 125 firefighters and 20 fire engines were sent to tackle the blaze. Photograph: Rasid Necati Aslim/Anadolu/Getty Images A nearby Amazon warehouse, separate from the industrial unit involved, was evacuated, according to PA Media. A London fire brigade assistant commissioner, Andy Pennick, said: “The brigade was called at 11.36[am] to reports of a fire on Hannah Close, Neasden. Upon arrival, firefighters were met by a well-developed fire involving a waste transfer facility. “Recognising the scale of the fire, the initial officer in attendance immediately requested 20 fire engines be mobilised to the scene. “An industrial unit, approximately 100 metres by 150 metres, was alight. At the height of the fire, around 125 firefighters were in attendance.” Pennick added: “This is a protracted incident that will see crews on scene for the remainder of the day as they work to fully extinguish the fire.” The LFB earlier said that the blaze was under control by about 5pm. Its cause was not yet known and was under investigation, the LFB added. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines UK Get the day’s headlines and highlights emailed direct to you every morning after newsletter promotion It is the third major fire at a recycling centre in London this summer. Earlier this month, about 100 firefighters responded to a blaze at a facility in Deptford , which involved about 50 tonnes of stored household waste. Fires at recycling centres caused by wrongly discarded lithium batteries, such as those found in vapes, are occurring at the rate of more than 10 a week, according to figures from the Environmental Services Association. Battery fires at waste facilities are estimated to cost £1bn a year and are causing growing frustration among fire chiefs. Europe Home page Europe 0 0 Poland restricts air traffic along its eastern border 03 September 2026 22:57 (UTC +04:00) Poland has decided to restrict air traffic in the eastern part of the country for three months. The measure is intended to help ensure the effective operation of the country’s air defense system, according to the Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces, APA reports citing RBC Ukraine. From September 10 to December 9, eastern Poland will be designated as a temporary restricted airspace zone, EP R134. The zone will extend from the ground to flight level FL95 — about 3 kilometers. Passenger aircraft normally fly at higher altitudes. "Therefore, the zone does not apply to passenger aircraft operating at higher altitudes," the military said. The restrictions are intended to ensure more effective operation of Poland’s military air defense system in the east, according to the command. (Russ Dillingham/Staff Photographer) Key Takeaways i Key Takeaways are written by Maine Trust staff and highlight the most important points of this article so you can get the gist at a glance. Auburn City Council voted in August to terminate its agreement with Flock Safety and request cameras and equipment be removed. Flock Safety initially responded to the city’s termination of the agreement, but did not address removal of cameras and equipment until Monday and are scheduling it. Should cameras and equipment remain in place, city officials said the city will remove them. AUBURN — Residents and city councilors have noted in recent weeks that license plate recognition cameras remain up around town about a month after the city’s agreement with Flock Safety was terminated and months after funding was removed for them from the city budget. That is about to change. City officials said Tuesday that Flock Safety officials reported that camera removal is being scheduled. “However they do not have a timeline for us right now,” said city spokesperson Liz Allen. “They understand the removal is overdue, and they are working to get this accomplished.” After removing funding for the cameras in May from the the city’s proposed 2026-27 budget the City Council terminated its contract with Flock Safety and requested cameras be removed in August. Related Auburn council leaves Flock camera funding out of proposed budget Because the terms of Auburn and Flock Safety’s agreement states equipment would be removed within a “commercially reasonable” period of time, the city has interpreted that time period to mean six to eight weeks, Allen said. Advertisement Should the cameras and equipment remain up at the end of that period, the city will remove them, Allen said. Flock data access and data sharing with surrounding law enforcement agencies ended when the agreement was terminated, Allen said. Auburn police began using Flock Safety cameras, acquired through a federal grant, in 2025. A $24,000 request by the police department in the 2027 budget to carry on the program was denied by the City Council when residents began airing concerns about the use of the technology. The cameras were installed by the department without public input or a council vote. Republican state lawmakers Laurel Libby and Quentin Chapman, both of Auburn, and David Boyer, of Poland, spearheaded a citizens initiative proposing a new ordinance banning the automatic license-plate-reading technology from Auburn streets. The petition drew 1,800 of the required 1,568 signatures , receiving over 1,200 signatures on Election Day in June alone. City councilors opted Sept. 21 not to adopt the ordinance, which automatically sent the matter to a special election to be held in four to six months. Related Auburn council sends Flock camera ban to voters City Councilor Rachel Randall of Ward 1 said she was pleased to learn the city has a clear next step to remove Flock Safety equipment, and that she will only be satisfied when the cameras are physically removed, not just turned off. “I’ve seen reports from other communities raising concerns about cameras being reconnected or reactivated without the municipality’s authorization, so for me, physical removal is important,” Randall said. Kelly Butler, Auburn City Ward 4 councilor, said Tuesday that it is important that, as a community, Auburn residents balance operational considerations with protecting the privacy of residents. People should expect the city is in a contractual process that takes time to reach completion, she said. “As we move through the process, information sharing with the community in a manner that offers clear confirmation of status of the equipment while the physical removal is underway is essential,” Butler said. “Overall, I think the shared goal here is to complete the contractual process (in a timely way), share accurate information with our community and assure our residents that their privacy is a priority to the city and council.” Joe Charpentier Staff Writer Joe Charpentier joined the Sun Journal in 2022 and covers the communities of Auburn, Lewiston and Poland. https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/masterche.text: Jess Phillips Updated Fri, October 9, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC 2 Tributes have flooded in for the chef (Image: BBC) Tributes have flooded in for a MasterChef star who has died at the age of just 44 after a battle with an aggressive brain tumour. The chef was rushed to hospital with a suspected stroke in January 2026, where he was told scans found a tumour on his brain in the right thalamus, above the brainstem. Tragically, though he underwent two surgeries, radiotherapy and rehabilitation, Mariusz Komenda has now sadly died, with the news confirmed on October 7. Mariusz starred in the eighth series of MasterChef Poland in 2019, where he reached the semi-final. He later returned as a guest and a judge to help other contestants on the show. He faced the "hardest fight of his life" this year after his diagnosis, with doctors removing a glioma from his brain in one surgery and taking out a piece of his skull in another. Mariusz was forced to start a fundraiser to help him afford travel for treatment, as well as the drugs and scans he needed, with a target of £31,000. Tributes have flooded in from Mariusz's former co-stars. 2019 series winner Grzegorz Zawierucha wrote: "Maniu... I can't manage to write anything. Goodbye, brother. See you. Prepare the most delicious dinner today, my friend." His co-star Mateusz Krojenka said he was "wrecked" by the news, praising Mariusz's "infectious smile". MasterChef star Mariusz Komenda has died (Image: TVN) MasterChef Poland said in a statement: "It is hard to find words that could express our grief. Mariusz, we will miss you very much." It added that Mariusz would be remembered for his "passion, energy and love of cooking". Mariusz opened Sztuka Restaurant in his hometown of roda lska, Poland. In April 2026 he also launched Mexican restaurant Father & Son with his son Mateusza.
